reconstructed_theorem_text: For all measurable W,X, with measurable singletons in W, every joint probability P on X times R, every K:W->X->R and b>0, assume for every q:W that K(q) has MemLp exponent 2 under PX=P.map Prod.fst and its L2(PX) class has norm at most b. Assume also MemLp(z->z.2,2,P) for the actual response coordinate. For every natural N>0, w:Fin N->W, i:Fin N, and u:W, use these literal definitions: PX=P.map Prod.fst; rho=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_j dirac(w(j)); rhoNew=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_j dirac(Function.update(w,i,u)(j)); predictor(law,x)=integral_W K(q,x) dlaw(q); risk(law)=integral_{X times R}(predictor(law,z.1)-z.2)^2 dP(z); potential(q)=2*integral_{X times R}(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)*K(q,z.1) dP(z); pairing=integral_W potential drhoNew-integral_W potential drho. Then all eleven claims hold: (1) 0<4*b^2; (2) rho is a probability measure; (3) rhoNew is a probability measure; (4) z->(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)^2 is integrable under P; (5) z->(predictor(rhoNew,z.1)-z.2)^2 is integrable under P; (6) potential is integrable under rho; (7) potential is integrable under rhoNew; (8) pairing=(N:R)^(-1)*(potential(u)-potential(w(i))); (9) risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-pairing=integral_X (predictor(rhoNew,x)-predictor(rho,x))^2 dPX(x); (10) 0<=risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-pairing; (11) risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-pairing<=4*b^2/(N:R)^2. All integrals are actual real Bochner integrals over the indicated whole spaces. The empirical predictors are pointwise finite arithmetic averages; the new one changes just index i, with difference (N:R)^(-1)*(K(u,x)-K(w(i),x)). Collisions are allowed and retain their index multiplicities. P is a joint law, not an assumed independent product; PX is its actual marginal and z.2 its actual response, with arbitrary dependence allowed. The supplied feature bound is uniform for every q in W and is an L2 bound, not a pointwise bound. Supplied memberships include almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite L2 seminorm. The response moment has no supplied uniform norm bound. Squared-loss and potential integrability, probability of the empirical measures, pairing, exact remainder, and bounds are derived, not additional assumptions. The loss is unhalved and potential has exact factor 2. The scalar pairing is new minus old of the same potential, never positive/truncated measure subtraction. The bound 4*b^2/N^2 is derived from the feature displacement bound 2*b/N; its numerator and normalized value are strictly positive, but the remainder may be zero. No global kernel measurability is imposed. Definitions exist syntactically for arbitrary laws via totalized integrals, while the analytic conclusions concern only these two finite empirical laws; no global differentiability or first-variation statement on arbitrary laws is asserted.
objects: W,X; actual joint probability P and actual marginal PX; raw scalar features and actual response coordinate; positive b,N; indexed particles, selected i and replacement u; two empirical measures; actual integral predictors, unhalved risks, rho-anchored potential, scalar pairing, and squared-displacement remainder.
domains: W,X are measurable with measurable singletons in W. P:Measure(X times R) has mass one. PX=P.map Prod.fst. K:W->X->R; b:R with b>0; N:N with N>0; w:Fin N->W; i:Fin N; u:W. Feature classes lie in real L2(PX) and response membership uses L2(P). All displayed integrals have real values.
quantifiers: For every stated space,P,K,b>0, assume every q has the displayed marginal L2 membership and norm bound, and assume joint response L2 membership. For every N>0,w,i,u define all quantities as displayed and conclude the full eleven-part conjunction. Uniform q quantification includes nonsampled locations; both sums use every j:Fin N.
assumptions: Supplied: joint probability P; b>0; every raw K(q) is in L2(PX) with class norm<=b; actual z.2 is in L2(P); N>0; measurable singletons. No independence, globally measurable kernel, distinct particles, pointwise feature bound, response norm bound, pre-assumed risk integrability, displacement budget, or first-variation regularity is given.
conclusion: (1) 0<4*b^2; (2) rho is a probability measure; (3) rhoNew is a probability measure; (4) z->(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)^2 is integrable under P; (5) z->(predictor(rhoNew,z.1)-z.2)^2 is integrable under P; (6) potential is integrable under rho; (7) potential is integrable under rhoNew; (8) pairing=(N:R)^(-1)*(potential(u)-potential(w(i))); (9) risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-pairing=integral_X (predictor(rhoNew,x)-predictor(rho,x))^2 dPX(x); (10) 0<=risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-pairing; (11) risk(rhoNew)-risk(rho)-pairing<=4*b^2/(N:R)^2. Definitions: PX=P.map Prod.fst; rho=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_j dirac(w(j)); rhoNew=(N:nonnegative_extended_reals)^(-1) times sum_j dirac(Function.update(w,i,u)(j)); predictor(law,x)=integral_W K(q,x) dlaw(q); risk(law)=integral_{X times R}(predictor(law,z.1)-z.2)^2 dP(z); potential(q)=2*integral_{X times R}(predictor(rho,z.1)-z.2)*K(q,z.1) dP(z); pairing=integral_W potential drhoNew-integral_W potential drho.
scopes: P governs joint loss and inner potential integrals, PX governs feature membership and the exact remainder, and the empirical laws govern parameter averages and outer potential integrals. The same potential based at rho is integrated twice with new-minus-old sign. Multiplicity m at a location gives mass m/N; updating i preserves all other indices even when values collide. Averaging occurs before squaring and there is no factor 1/2. Almost-everywhere feature classes support norm arguments, whereas empirical predictors use actual pointwise integral formulas. The two loss integrability conclusions and finite-law potential integrability are genuine. No analytic claim for arbitrary nonatomic laws or global first variation follows. N=0 and b<=0 are excluded by explicit hypotheses.
constant_dependencies: Index mass is exactly 1/N; the finite-update pairing uses real factor (N:R)^(-1). Potential has literal coefficient 2. The numerator 4*b^2 is strictly positive and the normalized budget is exactly 4*b^2/(N:R)^2, uniform in particles, update, and response moment. The exact remainder is nonnegative but need not be strictly positive; no hidden constants occur.
